case.believed: RequestFactory resolves django.urls.path converters and exercises middleware just like Client, and every JsonResponse accepts non-dict data and exposes response.json().
contract: assert JsonResponse accepts a dict by default, sets application/json, uses ordinary json.dumps spacing, and ASCII-escapes Unicode with its default encoder
assert JsonResponse rejects a list while safe=True and serializes it when safe=False
assert RequestFactory only builds a request: direct view invocation has no resolver match, path conversion, middleware marker, response header, or .json helper
assert Client resolves django.urls.path, converts an <int:item_id> segment to int, runs middleware, records resolver_match, and returns 404 when the converter does not match
assert json_dumps_params controls key order, separators, and Unicode escaping in the exact response bytes
assert Client response.json parses JSON responses but refuses text/plain based on the Content-Type header
case.goal: Use Django 6.1 JsonResponse and path routing without confusing RequestFactory with the full in-process Client stack
